sections.text_helper: Section 27.4.4 "AES symmetric cipher implementation" in chapter 27 (AES hardware accelerator (AES)), RM0522 Rev 1, page 795.
sections.section_content:
The AES hardware accelerator (AES) is a 32-bit AHB peripheral that encrypts or decrypts
16-byte blocks of data using the advanced encryption standard (AES). It also implements a
set of approved AES symmetric key security functions summarized in Table205. Those
functions can be certified NIST PUB 140-3.
[Table 205. AES approved symmetric key functions]
AES can be used directly by the CPU, or indirectly, using two DMA channels (one for the
plaintext, one for the ciphertext).
It is possible to suspend then resume any AES processing, following the sequence
described in Section27.4.8.
